utility pole noun

also telegraph pole, telephone pole, electricity pole, power pole

modern

Andresian p. 41
Traupman 308: ēlectricus

mālus ēlectricus

mālus, with a long ā, is an upright pole or beam (Front. Strat. 3.8.3), above all a ship’s mast, and the pole that held the awnings over a theatre (Lucr. 6.110; Liv. 39.7.8; all from Lewis & Short). Andresian is the only source for the phrase; Morgan–Owens has the heading telephone pole but no word.

See also pole.

SourcesLewis & Short: malus
